evidence.text: Matching lands with Invaders Ravage. Total the Damage: **1 per Explorer +2 per Town +3 per City**, then apply Defend and other explicit modifiers. Damage already marked on a piece does not reduce its outgoing Damage. Invaders deal the resulting Damage **equally, separately and simultaneously** to the land and its Dahan:

- **Dahan:** Every 2 Damage kills one Dahan; allocate efficiently to kill as many as possible, rather than spreading damage to keep all alive. If 1 remains after that, mark one surviving Dahan with 1 Damage. Return destroyed Dahan to supply.

Dahan do not shield the land; Damage to them is not subtracted from land Damage. **After Invader damage is fully resolved**, surviving Dahan each deal **2 Damage** to Invaders in that land, allocated by the players. A damaged surviving Dahan still deals 2. Surviving Dahan counterattack even when Invader Damage was reduced to zero by Defend, but not when the entire Ravage was skipped. Presence never counterattacks. If a Power changes Dahan Ravage Damage timing, that replaces their usual counterattack timing; each Dahan deals Ravage Damage only once. **Words of Warning** makes Dahan and Invader Ravage Damage simultaneous, so Dahan killed in that exchange still deal their Damage, with no second later counterattack. Losing Earth's defending Sacred Site to the resulting Blight does not retroactively remove its Defend from the simultaneous Damage to Dahan in that Ravage. [FAQ number-of-counterattacks-when-dahan-counterattack-early; .bu6oc8y]

**Destroy** returns pieces to supply regardless of Health when directly instructed. Every destroyed Town generates **1 Fear** and every destroyed City **2 Fear**, in addition to explicit Fear from the effect. Explorers generate none automatically. **Remove** returns the specified pieces without requiring Damage to reach their Health and without destruction Fear. Within the effect's count and piece-type restrictions, its decision-maker may choose any eligible pieces; there is no Explorer-first priority unless stated. **Replace** removes a piece and adds another, retaining its marked Damage: the replacement itself produces no Fear, but if the retained Damage destroys the new piece, destruction Fear applies normally. For simultaneous replacements, select all pieces before replacing any: the same original City cannot become a Town and then an Explorer within that one simultaneous instruction. Separate completed instructions or actions may replace the resulting piece again (e.g., successive players resolving **Trade Suffers** at Terror III).

grades.question: Must a land at Range 0 contain your Presence? Can a numeric Range boost waive a Sacred Site origin, a target-terrain restriction or the text “one of your lands”?

evidence.text: - The **targeting Range box** gives the maximum land distance from **one of your Presence**. Range 0 requires your Presence in the target land. Origin icons may require your Sacred Site or Presence in a particular terrain.

- **Range boosts:** Numeric Range boosts do not waive source/target restrictions or the requirement “one of your lands.” A Power still requiring your Sacred Site must have such an origin. General Power Range boosts affect Range values with a **printed Range arrow** in Powers **used by the Spirit receiving the bonus**, including effect-text arrows, subject to all restrictions. They do **not** increase the amount of another Range bonus: another boost cannot turn **Reaching Grasp**'s printed +2 into a larger bonus. They do not extend another Spirit's Powers merely because those Powers target the boosted Spirit. A bonus restricted to Powers does not extend Growth; Power Cards also resolve after normal Growth has finished. A special rule granting extra Range specifically for targeting lands with certain contents changes only the targeting Range box: **Shadows of the Dahan** does not extend effect-text Range arrows. grades.question: Can a Spirit give its unused Energy or Card Plays to another Spirit, or save unused Card Plays for the next turn? How does this differ from an explicit Power that grants another Spirit Energy or an extra play?

expected.answer: No ordinary sharing of individual Energy or Card Plays; Energy stays with its Spirit and can carry over, unused Card Plays expire. Explicit Power grants follow their instructions and can grant Energy or extra plays, but are not free sharing of the ordinary limits/resources.

observed.answer: Energy is individual and cannot ordinarily transfer; Card Plays cannot be shared or saved for a later turn. An explicit effect can grant another Spirit Energy, or an effect can explicitly allow an additional card play beyond the track limit; follow its wording.

evidence.text: **Gain Energy:** Take Energy equal to the **highest uncovered number** on your Energy/Turn track. Energy/Turn and Card Plays each use their own **highest uncovered value**; neither track adds its uncovered numbers together. Unspent Energy carries over between turns; it is individual and cannot ordinarily be transferred to another Spirit.

**Play and pay:** Play any number of cards from hand up to the highest uncovered Card Plays number, paying their printed Energy costs now, including Slow cards. Gain every played card's printed Elements immediately. No effects resolve yet and no targets need be committed yet. Card Plays cannot be shared or saved for a later turn. Energy expected from a Fast Power cannot pay these earlier Spirit-phase costs.

An effect explicitly letting you **play a card** outside the normal Spirit-phase play step grants an additional play beyond the track limit. Follow its payment instructions, gain Elements immediately, but resolve the new Power only in its appropriate speed phase when no other action is in progress, unless explicitly permitted to resolve immediately.

Retain changes to the Power, including extra Range or changed speed. An ordinary Repeat uses the Power's **most recently assigned speed**: a Slow Power repeats in Slow even if its permission came from a Fast Power; a formerly Fast Power explicitly made Slow before repeating now repeats in Slow. An instruction to Repeat immediately instead follows that explicit timing, directly after the originating use. [FAQ repeating-powers-with-changed-speeds] You may postpone choosing which eligible card to repeat until you actually repeat it, and make different choices/targets then. For **Powerstorm** and **Gift of Strength**, the Spirit receives a once-this-turn option rather than a grant-time selection of cards: a card played later that turn may be selected while it remains in play, subject to the permission’s restrictions and cost. [FAQ timing-of-choosing-powers-for-once-this-turn-repeats] Gift of Strength imposes its printed card-cost eligibility ceiling but requires no additional Energy payment for the Repeat, so an eligible card may be repeated with no Energy left. If the permission requires paying a cost, pay it as instructed. **Powerstorm** requires paying the repeated Power Card's Energy cost again when exercising each Repeat, including its threshold's further permissions; the original play payment does not cover it.

grades.question: A Blighted Island instruction simply tells each Spirit to destroy one of its Presence. May a Spirit choose a disk still covering its Presence track to uncover a benefit instead of destroying island Presence, and where does a destroyed disk go?

expected.answer: No. An unspecified instruction affecting Presence refers to that Spirit's Presence on the island, not track disks. Destroy an island disk and put it beside the island, not on the Spirit panel; no track benefit is uncovered by that loss.

observed.answer: A Blight instruction to destroy Presence means island Presence; it does not uncover track benefits. Destroyed Presence remains beside the island, not on the tracks.

evidence.text: A land with your Presence is **your land**. Your **Sacred Site** is a land with **two or more of your Presence**, not one disk each from different Spirits. Three or more still count as only one Sacred Site there. Any number of Spirits and disks can share a land. evidence.text: - **Range boosts:** Numeric Range boosts do not waive source/target restrictions or the requirement “one of your lands.” A Power still requiring your Sacred Site must have such an origin. grades.question: With Entwined Power’s threshold met, can only the target Spirit gift a card to the using Spirit, or may each gift one to the other? May a gifted card come from cards in play or personal discard instead of hand, and is either gift mandatory?

expected.answer: The using Spirit and target Spirit may each independently gift the other one Power Card from hand. Cards in play and in personal discard are ineligible. Either Spirit may decline its gift.
source_refs: /home/jonny/projects/boardgame-rules/docs/quality/summary-qa/spirit-island/2026-11-05-batch-002957/card-scope-source/entwined_power.jpg | all printed rules text in lower half; for Fear cards all three Terror panels | SHA256 2bb52d0c35e937676d641761ba10c33280694f2d540e8eb596889fc9f3b20325

observed.answer: At threshold, using and target Spirits may each independently gift the other one Power Card from hand. Cards in play/discard are ineligible; either gift is optional.

evidence.text: - **Entwined Power:** Shared Presence applies only to targeting (Range/source/target boxes), not to text effects or counting “your lands.” One disk each can count as a Sacred Site for their Power targeting, but is not a real shared site for Fear Cards or other effects. River's special Wetland-site rule remains River's own. For its base card gains, the **target Spirit** first makes the normal draw-four/keep-one gain; the **using Spirit** then gains one of those same three unkept cards, without drawing another four. In solo, both gains come from that single four-card draw. The threshold also lets the using and target Spirits each independently gift the other one Power Card **from hand**, optionally; cards in play or personal discard cannot be gifted by it. The threshold gives 6 Energy in solo; each Major gained still needs a separate Forget. If a transferred Unique references a special effect defined by a Spirit's rule, such as Drown, that definition still applies; skip instructions requiring a personal track you do not have. [Core: .3y28auq, .3y28aeu, .7w4g9jw, .7w4gee7, .7w4g8p9]

**Play and pay:** Play any number of cards from hand up to the highest uncovered Card Plays number, paying their printed Energy costs now, including Slow cards. Gain every played card's printed Elements immediately. No effects resolve yet and no targets need be committed yet. Card Plays cannot be shared or saved for a later turn. Energy expected from a Fast Power cannot pay these earlier Spirit-phase costs.

grades.question: If Powerstorm grants a Spirit a Repeat of a Power Card that it already paid to play, must that Spirit pay the card’s Energy cost again to use that Repeat?

expected.answer: Yes. To use a Repeat granted by Powerstorm, the target Spirit pays that repeated Power Card’s cost again. The same payment condition applies to each further Repeat granted by the threshold.
source_refs: /home/jonny/projects/boardgame-rules/docs/quality/summary-qa/spirit-island/2026-11-05-batch-002957/card-scope-source/powerstorm.jpg | all printed rules text in lower half; for Fear cards all three Terror panels | SHA256 ae19b1dbdc73f070f6a1e9f9973786547daae1de81a925d7db2e54da95f2e3bf

observed.answer: Powerstorm requires paying the repeated card’s printed Energy cost again when exercising the Repeat.

evidence.text: Retain changes to the Power, including extra Range or changed speed. An ordinary Repeat uses the Power's **most recently assigned speed**: a Slow Power repeats in Slow even if its permission came from a Fast Power; a formerly Fast Power explicitly made Slow before repeating now repeats in Slow. An instruction to Repeat immediately instead follows that explicit timing, directly after the originating use. [FAQ repeating-powers-with-changed-speeds] You may postpone choosing which eligible card to repeat until you actually repeat it, and make different choices/targets then. For **Powerstorm** and **Gift of Strength**, the Spirit receives a once-this-turn option rather than a grant-time selection of cards: a card played later that turn may be selected while it remains in play, subject to the permission’s restrictions and cost. [FAQ timing-of-choosing-powers-for-once-this-turn-repeats] Gift of Strength imposes its printed card-cost eligibility ceiling but requires no additional Energy payment for the Repeat, so an eligible card may be repeated with no Energy left. If the permission requires paying a cost, pay it as instructed. **Powerstorm** requires paying the repeated Power Card's Energy cost again when exercising each Repeat, including its threshold's further permissions; the original play payment does not cover it.

evidence.text: - **Drowning:** Ocean's rule Drowns Invaders/Dahan **after** they move into the Ocean on a board with Ocean's Presence; Ocean need not have a disk in the Ocean itself. Drown destroys: Town/City Fear happens immediately, and drowned Invaders go on Ocean's panel. At any time, trade stored Invaders: **X printed Health worth of drowned Invaders for 1 Energy**, X = number of Spirits; ignore Health modifiers and make change. They need not be exchanged when Drowned; Ocean may exchange them between actions during a later Spirit Phase, including before paying for cards. Dahan drowning gives no Energy. For these rules, **humans** means all Invaders (Explorers, Towns and Cities) and Dahan. Ordinary destruction, including thematically watery Powers, is not Drowning unless specified. If Ocean loses all Presence on that board mid-action, Ocean In Play lasts through the action tree; afterward non-human pieces left there remain physically but out of play until it returns. If a Drowning action fails to destroy its humans, **that same Drowning action** Pushes survivors to non-Ocean lands. This actual Push can trigger applicable movement effects; resolve the action and its triggers before completing the action tree. Humans cannot stay in the Ocean between action trees. Failed Drowning yields no Energy. **After the primary action and all triggered actions finish**, remaining illegal humans are cleaned up to the nearest legal land. At this post-action-tree stage, apply cleanup directly; the failed-Drowning Push belongs to the earlier action. evidence.text:
### Damage, Destroy, Remove, Replace and Defend

Use the named operation to determine what happens to the piece:

| Instruction | Effect on the piece |
| --- | --- |
| **Damage** | Mark Damage; reaching Health destroys the piece immediately. |
| **Destroy** | Return the specified piece to supply regardless of Health or marked Damage. |
| **Remove** | Take the specified piece off the board without a Damage-to-Health test. |
| **Replace** | Remove the original piece and put the specified new piece in its place, retaining marked Damage. |

“Damage” means **Damage to Invaders** unless explicitly stated otherwise. Normal Spirit Damage does not harm Dahan or the land. Distribute Damage among Invaders in the target land however you wish; Explorers need not be hit first. Damage from separate normal Powers and counterattacks can accumulate within a turn. A piece is destroyed immediately when its marked Damage reaches/exceeds its Health. Reduced Health can also destroy a previously damaged piece; Damage does not itself reduce Health. Marked Damage does not reduce the Health counted by a Health-worth removal allowance. If a damaged piece moves out of a Health bonus or into a Health penalty and is thereby destroyed, destruction occurs in its destination land, never in an in-between location. [FAQ if-an-invader-with-health-bonus-and-damage-is-moved-where-is-it-destroyed]

**Destroy** returns pieces to supply regardless of Health when directly instructed. Every destroyed Town generates **1 Fear** and every destroyed City **2 Fear**, in addition to explicit Fear from the effect. Explorers generate none automatically. **Remove** returns the specified pieces without requiring Damage to reach their Health and without destruction Fear. Within the effect's count and piece-type restrictions, its decision-maker may choose any eligible pieces; there is no Explorer-first priority unless stated. **Replace** removes a piece and adds another, retaining its marked Damage: the replacement itself produces no Fear, but if the retained Damage destroys the new piece, destruction Fear applies normally. For simultaneous replacements, select all pieces before replacing any: the same original City cannot become a Town and then an Explorer within that one simultaneous instruction. Separate completed instructions or actions may replace the resulting piece again (e.g., successive players resolving **Trade Suffers** at Terror III).

**Defend N** reduces each occurrence of Invader Damage to both land and Dahan by N for this turn, to a minimum of zero. Multiple Defend effects add. It does not reduce Spirit Damage or make Dahan do less counterattack Damage. Land and Dahan receive the reduction separately, not by splitting a shared allowance. A protection explicitly limited to Dahan is different: **Concealing Shadows** makes Dahan take no Damage from Ravaging Invaders this turn, while land still takes its normal Damage and can Blight. Protected surviving Dahan then counterattack normally. It does not protect them from direct Destroy instructions or Damage from other sources. [FAQ .7w4g8nu; original card text]

expected.answer: Terror I: no Invaders; II: no Towns/Cities; III: no Cities; earning final Fear card reveals Victory and wins without resolving it. Defeat: exhausted Blight pool as instructed (or board pool empty), any Spirit without island Presence, or need to draw Invader card from empty deck. Defeat occurs if any Spirit has no Presence on the island, the active Blight supply empties and says to lose, or an Explore must draw from an empty Invader deck. Finish a single-land Ravage’s action tree, including Dahan counterattack, then check outcomes: surviving Dahan can secure a sacrifice victory after the Spirit loses its last Presence. **Defeat routes:** Any Spirit has no Presence left on the island; the active Blight supply empties and its instructions say to lose (including the no-card board supply or final Blighted side); or you must draw an Invader card to Explore but none remains. A Healthy card's pool emptying usually flips it and refills according to its reverse, rather than immediately losing.

**Outcome timing (Living FAQ correction):** Finish the current action and all actions it triggers, including cascades and Dahan counterattack during a single-land Ravage, before checking victory/defeat. This is an **action tree**. Check before the next independent Power, next land's Invader action, or other separate action. If both win and loss are met at this check, the Spirits win a **sacrifice victory**. A final counterattack can therefore win despite losing the last Presence or Blight in that same Ravage. Do not finish Ravages in all other lands first. Players may choose which qualifying land Ravages first; a win at that land's completed action-tree check ends the game before any later Ravage. observed.answer: The Stage II Coastal Lands card affects all Coastal lands, not one terrain, for its listed action. Coastal lands Explore as matching lands and Build only with at least one Invader; Ravage only when Invaders are present. The card does not bypass those ordinary action requirements.

evidence.text: An empty action space does nothing. An Invader card affects all matching lands across the entire island, subject to its action's eligibility. A Stage III card with two terrains affects both; players may interleave lands of the two terrains. The Stage II **Coastal Lands** card affects all Coastal lands, not a terrain. **Ignore Stage II flag/Escalation icons without an Adversary.**

#### Build

In every matching land **with at least one Invader**, add exactly one building from supply:

- More Towns than Cities: add a **City**.

- Otherwise, including equal counts or only Explorers: add a **Town**.

Do not remove or upgrade an existing Town. Empty matching lands do not Build.

#### Explore

Add **one Explorer from supply** to every matching land which either contains a Town or City, or is adjacent to a Town, City, or Ocean. Existing pieces do not stop Explore; multiple sources still yield just one Explorer. Explorers do not act as sources. Land with no qualifying source is not Explored. Skipping actions in a neighboring land does not stop its Towns/Cities serving as sources for Explore elsewhere.

#### Ravage

Matching lands with Invaders Ravage. Total the Damage: **1 per Explorer +2 per Town +3 per City**, then apply Defend and other explicit modifiers. Damage already marked on a piece does not reduce its outgoing Damage. Invaders deal the resulting Damage **equally, separately and simultaneously** to the land and its Dahan:

- **Land:** If it takes **2 or more Damage**, add **one Blight**, regardless of how much more than 2. One Damage to land does nothing and is not saved for another action. Resolve Blight/Presence loss and cascading as described below.

- **Dahan:** Every 2 Damage kills one Dahan; allocate efficiently to kill as many as possible, rather than spreading damage to keep all alive. If 1 remains after that, mark one surviving Dahan with 1 Damage. Return destroyed Dahan to supply.

Dahan do not shield the land; Damage to them is not subtracted from land Damage. **After Invader damage is fully resolved**, surviving Dahan each deal **2 Damage** to Invaders in that land, allocated by the players. A damaged surviving Dahan still deals 2. Surviving Dahan counterattack even when Invader Damage was reduced to zero by Defend, but not when the entire Ravage was skipped. Presence never counterattacks. If a Power changes Dahan Ravage Damage timing, that replaces their usual counterattack timing; each Dahan deals Ravage Damage only once. **Words of Warning** makes Dahan and Invader Ravage Damage simultaneous, so Dahan killed in that exchange still deal their Damage, with no second later counterattack. Losing Earth's defending Sacred Site to the resulting Blight does not retroactively remove its Defend from the simultaneous Damage to Dahan in that Ravage. [FAQ number-of-counterattacks-when-dahan-counterattack-early; .bu6oc8y]

Invaders and Dahan sharing a land do not automatically fight at other times.

Example: A Town, Explorer and two Dahan with no Defend cause 3 land Damage (one Blight), and simultaneously 3 Dahan Damage (one dead, one damaged). The survivor can destroy the Town for 1 Fear. [CORE pp.9,11]

grades.question: What is the order of the Invader Phase, and if a Blighted Island start-of-phase effect destroys a Spirit’s last Presence, may an earned Fear Card resolve first to avert defeat?

expected.answer: Resolve Blighted Island instructions first, then earned Fear, Ravage, Build, Explore and advance Invader cards. Finish the Blighted effect action tree and check outcomes before Fear; if a Spirit still has no island Presence and no win condition is met then, lose without resolving the later Fear card. Cannot reorder to avert loss.

requested_parts: whether Fear resolves before last-Presence Blighted loss
observed.answer: Invader Phase order is Blighted Island, Fear, Ravage, Build, Explore, advance cards. Outcomes are checked after an action tree before the next independent action; if the Blighted Island effect destroys the last Presence and completes its action tree, defeat is checked before the separate Fear step, so a Fear card does not resolve first to avert it.

evidence.text:
### 3. Invader Phase

1. **Blighted Island:** If the Blight Card is Blighted, follow its instructions at the specified timing (typically start of each Invader Phase). No such step applies with the printed no-card pool.

2. **Fear:** Turn the earned face-down stack over and resolve its cards **in the order earned**, one at a time, without looking ahead. Use **only the current Terror Level's effect**, even if the card was earned at a lower level. Discard each resolved card to Fear discard. Fear earned during this step can earn more cards: append them to the bottom of the resolving stack and resolve them this same step. Subsequent cards use any newly reached Terror Level. Fear earned later, such as in Ravage or Slow, waits for the next Fear step.

3. **Ravage:** Resolve the card in Ravage, if any.

4. **Build:** Resolve the card in Build, if any.

5. **Explore:** Reveal the next Invader card and resolve Explore. If a card must be drawn and the deck is empty, lose. Revealing the last existing card is not itself a loss.

6. **Advance cards:** Discard the old Ravage card; slide Build to Ravage and the just-revealed Explore card to Build.

An empty action space does nothing. An Invader card affects all matching lands across the entire island, subject to its action's eligibility. A Stage III card with two terrains affects both; players may interleave lands of the two terrains. The Stage II **Coastal Lands** card affects all Coastal lands, not a terrain. **Ignore Stage II flag/Escalation icons without an Adversary.**

Before resolving the actions from a card, determine which lands qualify; players choose the order of those lands. Changes during the card do not add newly eligible lands to that list. Determine eligibility anew for each later card, so a land newly occupied during an earlier Ravage card can Ravage under a later matching Ravage card. In a land already due to Ravage, newly arrived Invaders participate when its Ravage resolves. Resolve each land fully, including cascades and triggered effects, and check outcomes before proceeding to the next. [CORE pp.9–10; FAQ pieces-added-or-moved-by-ravages-do-not-cause-more-ravages; .9v5kaam]

#### Ravage

Matching lands with Invaders Ravage. Total the Damage: **1 per Explorer +2 per Town +3 per City**, then apply Defend and other explicit modifiers. Damage already marked on a piece does not reduce its outgoing Damage. Invaders deal the resulting Damage **equally, separately and simultaneously** to the land and its Dahan:

- **Land:** If it takes **2 or more Damage**, add **one Blight**, regardless of how much more than 2. One Damage to land does nothing and is not saved for another action. Resolve Blight/Presence loss and cascading as described below.

- **Dahan:** Every 2 Damage kills one Dahan; allocate efficiently to kill as many as possible, rather than spreading damage to keep all alive. If 1 remains after that, mark one surviving Dahan with 1 Damage. Return destroyed Dahan to supply.

Dahan do not shield the land; Damage to them is not subtracted from land Damage. **After Invader damage is fully resolved**, surviving Dahan each deal **2 Damage** to Invaders in that land, allocated by the players. A damaged surviving Dahan still deals 2. Surviving Dahan counterattack even when Invader Damage was reduced to zero by Defend, but not when the entire Ravage was skipped. Presence never counterattacks. If a Power changes Dahan Ravage Damage timing, that replaces their usual counterattack timing; each Dahan deals Ravage Damage only once. **Words of Warning** makes Dahan and Invader Ravage Damage simultaneous, so Dahan killed in that exchange still deal their Damage, with no second later counterattack. Losing Earth's defending Sacred Site to the resulting Blight does not retroactively remove its Defend from the simultaneous Damage to Dahan in that Ravage. [FAQ number-of-counterattacks-when-dahan-counterattack-early; .bu6oc8y]

Invaders and Dahan sharing a land do not automatically fight at other times.

Example: A Town, Explorer and two Dahan with no Defend cause 3 land Damage (one Blight), and simultaneously 3 Dahan Damage (one dead, one damaged). The survivor can destroy the Town for 1 Fear. [CORE pp.9,11]

#### Build

In every matching land **with at least one Invader**, add exactly one building from supply:

- More Towns than Cities: add a **City**.

- Otherwise, including equal counts or only Explorers: add a **Town**.

Do not remove or upgrade an existing Town. Empty matching lands do not Build.

#### Explore

Add **one Explorer from supply** to every matching land which either contains a Town or City, or is adjacent to a Town, City, or Ocean. Existing pieces do not stop Explore; multiple sources still yield just one Explorer. Explorers do not act as sources. Land with no qualifying source is not Explored. Skipping actions in a neighboring land does not stop its Towns/Cities serving as sources for Explore elsewhere.

**Outcome timing (Living FAQ correction):** Finish the current action and all actions it triggers, including cascades and Dahan counterattack during a single-land Ravage, before checking victory/defeat. This is an **action tree**. Check before the next independent Power, next land's Invader action, or other separate action. If both win and loss are met at this check, the Spirits win a **sacrifice victory**. A final counterattack can therefore win despite losing the last Presence or Blight in that same Ravage. Do not finish Ravages in all other lands first. Players may choose which qualifying land Ravages first; a win at that land's completed action-tree check ends the game before any later Ravage. Earning Fear reveals Terror dividers immediately; use their new conditions at the next outcome check. [CORE p.12; FAQ .bu6oc8v, .9v5kfq7]

grades.question: A Power's own threshold gives it +1 Range. If the threshold is met on both the original use and its Repeat, does the Repeat get +2 Range? If that threshold is no longer met on the Repeat, is the first +1 retained?

expected.answer: Do not stack the same internal Range boost a second time: the Repeat retains the original +1, not +2. It retains that Range modification even if the threshold is no longer met when repeating.

requested_parts: whether repeated +1 Range threshold stacks to +2
whether previously granted +1 retained if threshold later unqualified
observed.answer: The Power’s Range change carries to a Repeat, but the same threshold Range bonus does not stack again to make +2. The earlier +1 remains on the Repeat even if the threshold is no longer met.

evidence.text: - **Repeat limits:** **Powerstorm** and **Gift of Strength** repeat Power **Cards**, not Innates. Powerstorm's threshold repeats up to three **different** cards. A Range/Speed change granted by a threshold carries to a Repeat even if that threshold is no longer met; it does not stack the same Range bonus again. [Core: .3y28aex, .7w4g8q9, Repeating-internal-range-boosts]

Retain changes to the Power, including extra Range or changed speed. An ordinary Repeat uses the Power's **most recently assigned speed**: a Slow Power repeats in Slow even if its permission came from a Fast Power; a formerly Fast Power explicitly made Slow before repeating now repeats in Slow. An instruction to Repeat immediately instead follows that explicit timing, directly after the originating use. [FAQ repeating-powers-with-changed-speeds] You may postpone choosing which eligible card to repeat until you actually repeat it, and make different choices/targets then. grades.question: An effect explicitly adds two Blight simultaneously to one land containing two Presence from each of two Spirits. Counting only Presence destroyed in that land by this one addition, how many disks does each Spirit lose? Would adding one Blight there in each of two separate completed instructions destroy Presence once or twice, assuming each Spirit still has Presence there?

expected.answer: The simultaneous addition destroys one Presence from each Spirit, even though two Blight tokens are added. Two separate additions destroy one Presence per Spirit on each addition, hence two per Spirit if available. Cascades elsewhere are outside the requested count.

requested_parts: Presence losses from two simultaneous Blight in land with 2 disks each
losses across two separate completed additions
observed.answer: One Blight event, even adding two Blight simultaneously, destroys one Presence per Spirit in that land, so each loses one disk. Two separate completed additions each cause one Presence loss per Spirit, so each loses two total if still present there for both.

evidence.text:
### Blight procedure

After setup, take Blight added to the island from the active card/board pool. Whenever one or more Blight is added to a land:

1. Destroy **one Presence from each Spirit** with Presence there, not every disk and not just one disk total. Decrease each affected Spirit's Presence count in that land by exactly one.

2. If the land already had any Blight, **cascade**: also add **one** Blight to **one adjacent land** chosen by the players. Resolve its Presence loss and cascade if it was already Blighted. The amount of existing Blight does not multiply the cascade. Cascades can cross boards and remain part of the original action; revisiting a land destroys another disk per Spirit there and continues cascading.

The original land still receives its Blight; cascading does not replace it. If a pool empties during this process, immediately follow the card's instructions, flip/refill as directed and continue unfinished Blight additions/cascades. Add the reverse side's printed number per Spirit from the box; **do not add the initial +1 again**. If an instruction must add more Blight **simultaneously** than remains on Healthy, flip immediately before that addition, carry the remaining old Blight into the newly created pool and fully resolve any immediate flip effects as nested actions, then return to add the required Blight. Do not add the setup +1 again. [FAQ .9v5kfqt]

Blighted card effects apply at their printed timing. Without a card, the printed board pool empties into defeat at the action-tree outcome check.

Removing island Blight returns it to whichever side of the card is currently face-up (or the board pool if no card). A Blighted card never becomes Healthy again, however much Blight is removed. Removing Blight does not restore destroyed Presence.

grades.question: Spirit A has an existing +2 bonus to its Power Ranges and uses Reaching Grasp, whose text grants target Spirit B +2 Range with all their Powers. Does A’s existing bonus increase the amount granted to +4, or does B receive +2? Does B’s Power-only bonus cover Innate Powers as well as Power Cards, and can it extend ordinary Growth placement?

expected.answer: The grant stays +2; Range boosts do not increase another Range boost. Reaching Grasp’s Power-only bonus applies to B’s Powers, including Innates and Power Cards, subject to the normal Range-arrow restrictions. It does not extend ordinary Growth, which is not a Power; Power Cards also resolve after normal Growth.
source_refs: Primary original Reaching Grasp face: card-scope-source/reaching_grasp.jpg

whether B Power-only bonus covers Innates and Cards
observed.answer: A’s existing bonus does not increase Reaching Grasp’s printed +2; B receives +2. The Power-only bonus applies to B’s Power Cards and Innate Powers, but not ordinary Growth placement.

evidence.text: - **Range boosts:** Numeric Range boosts do not waive source/target restrictions or the requirement “one of your lands.” A Power still requiring your Sacred Site must have such an origin. General Power Range boosts affect Range values with a **printed Range arrow** in Powers **used by the Spirit receiving the bonus**, including effect-text arrows, subject to all restrictions. They do **not** increase the amount of another Range bonus: another boost cannot turn **Reaching Grasp**'s printed +2 into a larger bonus. They do not extend another Spirit's Powers merely because those Powers target the boosted Spirit. A bonus restricted to Powers does not extend Growth; Power Cards also resolve after normal Growth has finished. A special rule granting extra Range specifically for targeting lands with certain contents changes only the targeting Range box: **Shadows of the Dahan** does not extend effect-text Range arrows. [Core: special-rule-range-bonuses-to-targeting; official FAQ: [Range boosts](https://querki.net/raw/darker/spirit-island-faq/What-do-range-boosts-affect)] [Core: .3y28aqg, .7w4g8nq]

grades.question: Wrap in Wings of Sunlight meets its threshold. Its target land initially has no Dahan, but Dahan are available in adjacent lands. expected.answer: Wrap’s explicit First instruction Gathers before the base Move, allowing those gathered Dahan to be moved by the base effect and Defend 5 in the destination if at least one moves. Dissolve’s explicit Before Pushing instruction resolves its threshold Damage before the Explorer Push (after the preceding replacements). Such timing words override the default top-to-bottom position; they do not create another Power use.

observed.answer: Wrap’s “First, Gather up to 3 Dahan” threshold resolves before its base Move, so gathered Dahan can then be moved and allow the destination’s Defend. Dissolve’s threshold specifies Invaders damage simultaneously before the Explorer Push.

evidence.text: - **Location-dependent effects:** **Wrap in Wings of Sunlight** resolves its threshold’s **First, Gather up to 3 Dahan** before its base Move; those gathered Dahan may then move and allow the destination’s Defend. It grants no Defend if zero Dahan move: there is no moved-to land. Moving Dahan to their original land can count as Move if the Power permits. **Blazing Renewal** permits its target Spirit to add its destroyed Presence directly to one legal island land, not to tracks. Its printed “adds 2” is mandatory to the extent possible, using the Power user's Presence for its internal Range; it cannot deal threshold Damage with no destroyed Presence restored: “that land” refers to where it adds Presence. **The Trees and Stones Speak of War** deals 1 Damage per Dahan and grants Defend 2 per Dahan in its target land. Its threshold moves Defend 2 with each Dahan it Pushes, leaving the remaining Defend in the target. Each destination receives Defend 2 for each Dahan this Power Pushes into it. Only this Power's Defend 2 per pushed Dahan travels; separate Defend from another effect, such as Words of Warning, stays in its original land. A later Power moving those Dahan does not carry that Defend. [Core: .9v5kfqd, .9v5kfr0, .bu6oc8n, .bu6ocxq]

- **Core Power specifics:** **Song of Sanctity** is Slow, despite missing cost-circle ink in some printings. For three use the triangular layout, and for four the two-row parallelogram layout illustrated in CORE pp.6–7. [FAQ .7w4g8pg] Populate every land with its printed Invader, Dahan and Blight setup icons. Setup Blight comes from the box, never the Blight pool, and does not cascade or destroy Presence.

### Blight procedure

After setup, take Blight added to the island from the active card/board pool. Whenever one or more Blight is added to a land:

1. Destroy **one Presence from each Spirit** with Presence there, not every disk and not just one disk total. Decrease each affected Spirit's Presence count in that land by exactly one.

2. If the land already had any Blight, **cascade**: also add **one** Blight to **one adjacent land** chosen by the players. Resolve its Presence loss and cascade if it was already Blighted. The amount of existing Blight does not multiply the cascade. Cascades can cross boards and remain part of the original action; revisiting a land destroys another disk per Spirit there and continues cascading.

The original land still receives its Blight; cascading does not replace it. If a pool empties during this process, immediately follow the card's instructions, flip/refill as directed and continue unfinished Blight additions/cascades. Add the reverse side's printed number per Spirit from the box; **do not add the initial +1 again**. If an instruction must add more Blight **simultaneously** than remains on Healthy, flip immediately before that addition, carry the remaining old Blight into the newly created pool and fully resolve any immediate flip effects as nested actions, then return to add the required Blight. Do not add the setup +1 again. [FAQ .9v5kfqt]

Blighted card effects apply at their printed timing. Without a card, the printed board pool empties into defeat at the action-tree outcome check.

Removing island Blight returns it to whichever side of the card is currently face-up (or the board pool if no card). A Blighted card never becomes Healthy again, however much Blight is removed. Removing Blight does not restore destroyed Presence.

requested_parts: whether Ocean may exchange stored Invaders between later Spirit-phase actions before paying
observed.answer: Yes. Ocean may trade stored Invaders between actions during a later Spirit Phase, including before paying for cards; no new Drowning is required.

evidence.text: - **Drowning:** Ocean's rule Drowns Invaders/Dahan **after** they move into the Ocean on a board with Ocean's Presence; Ocean need not have a disk in the Ocean itself. Drown destroys: Town/City Fear happens immediately, and drowned Invaders go on Ocean's panel. At any time, trade stored Invaders: **X printed Health worth of drowned Invaders for 1 Energy**, X = number of Spirits; ignore Health modifiers and make change. They need not be exchanged when Drowned; Ocean may exchange them between actions during a later Spirit Phase, including before paying for cards. Dahan drowning gives no Energy. For these rules, **humans** means all Invaders (Explorers, Towns and Cities) and Dahan. Ordinary destruction, including thematically watery Powers, is not Drowning unless specified. If Ocean loses all Presence on that board mid-action, Ocean In Play lasts through the action tree; afterward non-human pieces left there remain physically but out of play until it returns. If a Drowning action fails to destroy its humans, **that same Drowning action** Pushes survivors to non-Ocean lands. This actual Push can trigger applicable movement effects; resolve the action and its triggers before completing the action tree. Humans cannot stay in the Ocean between action trees. Failed Drowning yields no Energy. **After the primary action and all triggered actions finish**, remaining illegal humans are cleaned up to the nearest legal land. At this post-action-tree stage, apply cleanup directly; the failed-Drowning Push belongs to the earlier action. Cleanup is not an action, move, removal or destruction and triggers nothing, and occurs before the outcome check. If no legal land exists return humans to supply as cleanup. requested_parts: whether same Town can generate Bringer Fear more than once within one Tsunami use
observed.answer: Only once. Within a single Power use, a given Invader can be pretend-destroyed once, even if the Town is pushed to another affected land and would be destroyed there again.

evidence.text: - **Bringer of Dreams and Nightmares:** Its Powers' explicit Damage/Destroy cannot actually harm Invaders/Dahan or destroy anything except its own Presence. This restriction still applies when that Power's Damage/Destroy instruction names Dahan or another Spirit as the actor. An explicit instruction to Damage or Destroy Dahan does nothing to those Dahan; skip that instruction and resolve the rest of the Power normally. For each Power use, evaluate what it would destroy if resolved normally: generate **0 Fear per Explorer, 2 per Town, 5 per City**, and Push the would-be-destroyed Explorers/Towns. This special rule does not Push Cities. No real Damage is marked, so different Powers or a Repeat cannot combine their hypothetical Damage; multiple instructions **within one Power** can. Existing real Damage from others helps its hypothetical destruction and remains unchanged afterward. Within a single Power use, a given Invader can be pretend-destroyed only once. Repeats can “destroy” the same piece again for Fear. It does not get bonuses conditional on **actual** destruction (e.g., Mists of Oblivion or Vengeance of the Dead) from these pretend destructions. [Core: .7w4g9jv, .7w4g7yx, .7w4g7yu, .7w4g8pj, .9v5kfh3, .9v5katc, .bu6oc6g]

requested_parts: whether turning unearned Fear Card face-up earns or resolves it
observed.answer: No. Turning it face-up only previews the card; it neither earns it nor resolves its Fear effect early. Normal earning and resolution still apply.

evidence.text: - **Bringer's exceptions:** Fear Cards and Dahan counterattacks after its Defend deal real Damage, because they are not its Power's Damage. Bringer can Remove/Replace, add real Blight (destroying Presence normally), modify Invader actions or cause actual Ravage. Reducing Health or replacing a damaged piece with a lower-Health one can cause real destruction by core Health rules. If Bringer Pushes a “destroyed” Town into Ocean, Ocean's separate Drowning destroys it: **3 total Fear** (2 from Bringer, 1 from Ocean). **Spirits May Yet Dream** may turn any face-down Fear Card face-up, whether already earned or anywhere in the deck. This only previews the card: turning it face-up neither earns it nor resolves its Fear effect early; normal earning and resolution still apply. Its Element-granting level gives the target Spirit one Element of a type it already has at least one of; it cannot grant a currently absent Element type.
